# Law of Large Numbers

The LLN guarantees that empirical averages converge to expectations — the mathematical foundation of statistical learning.

## Weak LLN (WLLN)

For iid Xᵢ with E[X]=μ, Var(X)=σ²<∞:

**X̄ₙ →_p μ**: P(|X̄ₙ−μ|>ε) → 0 for any ε>0

Convergence in probability — the distribution of X̄ₙ concentrates around μ.

## Chebyshev's Inequality Proof

Chebyshev: P(|Y−μ_Y|≥ε) ≤ σ²_Y/ε²

Apply to X̄ₙ: Var(X̄ₙ) = σ²/n →

**P(|X̄ₙ−μ|≥ε) ≤ σ²/(nε²) → 0** as n→∞ □

Rate: O(1/n) for probability. CLT gives much sharper e^(−nε²/(2σ²))/√n rate.

## Strong LLN (SLLN)

If E[|X|]<∞ (only finite mean needed):

**P(lim_{n→∞} X̄ₙ = μ) = 1** — almost sure convergence

Every sample path converges, not just in distribution.

| Mode | Meaning | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| In distribution (CLT) | CDFs converge | Weakest |
| In probability (WLLN) | P(\|X̄−μ\|>ε)→0 | Medium |
| Almost surely (SLLN) | Every path converges | Strong |

## Convergence Rates

- **Chebyshev**: P(error>ε) ≤ σ²/(nε²) — O(1/n)
- **CLT**: P(error>ε) ≈ 2Φ(−ε√n/σ) — exponential in n
- **Hoeffding** (bounded Xᵢ∈[a,b]): P(error>ε) ≤ 2exp(−2nε²/(b−a)²) — non-asymptotic!

Hoeffding is the bound used in PAC learning theory — holds for all n, no σ required.

## Monte Carlo — LLN as Foundation

Î_N = (1/N)Σf(xᵢ) →_a.s. E_p[f(X)] by SLLN

The validity of Monte Carlo integration IS the law of large numbers.

Var(Î_N) = σ²_f/N → 0, MSE → 0. SE = σ_f/√N.

```python
# Demonstrate LLN convergence rate
mu, sigma, epsilon = 0, 1, 0.2
for n in [10, 50, 100, 500, 1000]:
    X_bars = np.mean(np.random.randn(100000, n), axis=1)
    actual = np.mean(np.abs(X_bars) > epsilon)
    chebyshev = sigma**2 / (n * epsilon**2)
    clt = 2 * stats.norm.sf(epsilon * np.sqrt(n) / sigma)
    print(f"n={n}: actual={actual:.5f}, Chebyshev={chebyshev:.5f}, CLT={clt:.5f}")
```

## Empirical Risk Minimisation — LLN as Foundation

ERM minimises: R̂_n(f) = (1/n)Σℓ(f(xᵢ),yᵢ) as proxy for R(f) = E[ℓ(f(X),Y)]

By SLLN: R̂_n(f) →_a.s. R(f) for fixed f and iid data.

**PAC bound** (uniform LLN over function class F with VC dimension d):

P(sup_{f∈F}|R(f)−R̂_n(f)|>ε) ≤ 4·(2n)^d · e^(−nε²/8)

Sample complexity: n = O(d/ε² · log(1/δ)) — LLN rate × capacity of F.

**Why more data helps**: SE(R̂_n) = σ/√n. Doubling n halves the SE. Large model capacity d → larger required n.

## LLN and Test Set Validity

Test set accuracy (1/n_test)Σ(f(xᵢ)==yᵢ) →_p P(f(X)==Y) by LLN.

This IS the entire mathematical justification for held-out evaluation. Test set contamination (using test data for model selection) violates the iid assumption and biases the estimate.

## Non-iid Extensions

- **Time series**: correlations reduce effective n but LLN holds for mixing processes
- **Federated learning**: non-iid clients — federated averaging may not converge to true optimum
- **Minibatch SGD**: minibatch gradient →_p true gradient as B→∞ — justifies linear LR scaling rule
